title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 144
paragraphs: The reason the Ionians established exactly twelve cities, refusing to admit any more, was that when they lived in the Peloponnese they had been divided into twelve parts—just as the Achaeans who drove them out are divided into twelve parts today. First is Pellene, nearest to Sicyon, then Aigeira and Aigai (where the ever-flowing river Crathis rises, from which the river of the same name in Italy takes its name), then Bura, Helike (where the Ionians fled after being defeated by the Achaeans), Aigion, Rhypes, Patrae, Pharae, Olenos (where the great river Peiros flows), Dyme, and Tritaeae—the only inland city of the twelve. These formed the twelve divisions of the Ionians in old times, and these are the twelve divisions of the Achaeans now.
